metadata.title: Choosing a queue for background jobs

content.label: Why the billing queue is changing
content.takeaway: In-process workers lose queued jobs on every deploy or crash.

nodes.title: Deploys and crashes lose queued jobs

content.markdown:
About 40,000 background jobs a day (invoice PDFs, receipt emails, webhook retries) run in an in-process worker pool. A deploy or a crash loses any job queued but not yet started: last quarter, 37 invoice emails.

Peak load is 600 jobs per minute, during the month-end billing run.

content.label: Three options compared
content.takeaway: Costs differ in kind: per-request pricing, fixed machines, or spare database capacity.

nodes.title: Monthly cost and effort by option

rows: The provider handles storage, scaling and redelivery; workers poll for messages
Priced per million requests; assumes current volume, roughly $900 a month at three times today's volume
Three virtual machines we install, patch and monitor
about 12 hours (an estimate: no one on the team has run this broker in production)
Flat until the cluster needs a fourth machine
A jobs table in the billing Postgres database; workers claim rows with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
Uses spare capacity on the existing primary

content.label: Trade-offs by option
content.takeaway: Each option's main benefit comes with a condition the team would have to meet.

nodes.title: Managed queue: least operational work, at-least-once delivery

content.markdown:
Almost no operational work; failed messages move to a dead-letter queue automatically.

**Conditions**
- Delivers each message at least once, so every job handler must be made idempotent before switching; today only the email handler is.
- Ties us to one provider's API; the local emulator doesn't support dead-lettering.

nodes.title: Self-hosted broker: priorities and delays, unproven to run

content.markdown:
Priority queues and delayed delivery would let month-end invoices jump ahead of webhook retries.

**Conditions**
- No one on the team has run this broker in production.
- Upgrades need a maintenance window.

nodes.title: Job table: enqueue in the same transaction, extra load on the primary

content.markdown:
A job is written in the same transaction as the billing change that causes it, so it can't be lost between commit and enqueue.

**Conditions**
- Only covers jobs created inside the billing database transaction; jobs from the reporting service, which has its own database, don't get it.
- Polling adds read load to the primary database, the main risk at month-end.

content.label: Selection criteria
content.takeaway: Two must-haves gate every option; four weighted criteria score the rest.

nodes.title: Must-haves: no lost jobs, 1,800 jobs per minute

content.markdown:
An option that fails either is out, regardless of its score:
1. No job is lost when a worker crashes or the service is deployed.
2. Absorbs 1,800 jobs per minute (three times today's peak) without manual intervention.

- Operational effort: 40%
- Monthly cost: 30%
- Developer experience, including local testing: 20%
- Portability away from our cloud provider: 10%

content.label: Evidence so far
content.takeaway: Only the job table has been load-tested, and not at the required rate.

nodes.title: Job table held 1,200 a minute, strained at 2,000

content.markdown:
On a staging copy with synthetic jobs: 1,200 jobs per minute sustained at a p95 claim latency of 18 ms. At 2,000 jobs per minute, primary CPU reached 85% and p95 latency rose to 240 ms.

**Limits**
- 1,800 jobs per minute was not tested.
- Staging is about a quarter of production size, so the results may not carry over.

nodes.title: Managed queue and broker are untested by us

content.markdown: Neither was load-tested. The provider documents throughput far above our peak for the managed queue, but that is the provider's figure, not ours.

content.label: Decision status: deferred
content.takeaway: No option is chosen until the job table is load-tested at the required rate.

nodes.title: Decision deferred until the 1,800 a minute measurement

content.markdown:
This note does not recommend an option. The decision waits until the job table is measured at 1,800 jobs per minute on a production-sized database.

**Open requirement per option**
- Managed queue: every job handler made idempotent.
- Self-hosted broker: a named owner for broker on-call and upgrades.
- Job table: a passing load test at 1,800 jobs per minute.

items.text: Priya: bring the load-test result to the next architecture review
